title: Project: build the whole thing
objectives: plan a feature before writing it
assemble prompt, call, parse and guard into one flow
handle the paths where it goes wrong
say what you would check before showing anyone

steps.instruction: Nine lessons of pieces. Now build one real feature: a note tagger.

pipeline.label: your guard
pipeline.note: signed in, not empty, not enormous

pipeline.label: your check
pipeline.note: parsed, and one of your real tags

pipeline.label: the browser
pipeline.note: shows the tag, or nothing at all

body: Notes go in. One tag comes back, from a list you control.
Six stops. Only one of them is the model, and the other five are the reason it works.
steps.keypoint: The model is one step in the middle. The engineering is everything around it.

steps.instruction: Put the build in order. Tap the steps into the sequence you would write them.
lines: Guard the input: signed in, not empty, not too long
Write the system prompt: task, allowed tags, JSON only
Send the note as a user message
Parse the reply safely, never throwing
Check the tag is one of yours
Show the tag, or show nothing
steps.after: Guard first, because everything after it costs money. Check last, because the model is a suggestion, not a decision.
steps.keypoint: Guard, prompt, send, parse, check, show.

steps.instruction: An empty note arrives. What should happen first?
steps.after: An empty note is a free call you were about to pay for.
opts: Ask the model to handle it
steps.why: An empty note is a call you were about to pay for that could not possibly produce a useful tag.

steps.instruction: The prompt asks for JSON with no fences. What comes back?
steps.after: Clean JSON, first time, because you asked for it properly. A1.5 and A1.7 in one line.
steps.why: Clean JSON, because the prompt asked for it properly. A1.5 and A1.7 in a single line.

steps.instruction: Tagging runs on every note a student saves. Which model?
steps.code: const request = { model: "?", max_tokens: 20, messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Chemistry test Thursday." }] };
opts: small, it is one step and it runs constantly
steps.why: Tagging is a single-step job on a short input, and it happens on every save. That is exactly the shape the cheap fast model is built for. A1.3.
steps.after: High volume, simple job. The answer is the same every time.
steps.keypoint: Volume plus simplicity means the small model.

steps.after: It parsed. And on the day it does not, this prints unavailable instead of taking the page down.
body: On the day the reply is malformed, this prints unavailable instead of taking the page down.

steps.instruction: This version trusts the model completely. Tap the line that does it.
steps.why: It writes whatever came back straight into your database, with no check that it is one of your real tags. One odd reply and your tag list quietly grows a category nobody made.
steps.after: The model suggested. Your code committed. That gap is where the check belongs.
steps.keypoint: Never write a model's output into your data without checking it first.

steps.instruction: The model suggested Paris. Your tags are chemistry, physics, history. What prints?
steps.after: The model was confident and wrong. Your one line caught it. A1.2, doing its job.
steps.why: Not one of yours, so it does not go in. Without this line, Paris quietly becomes a tag nobody created.

steps.instruction: max_tokens was 2, so the reply was truncated. What prints?
steps.after: A cap set too low produces half a word. Now it produces a handled case.
steps.why: stop_reason was max_tokens, so the text is half a word. Checking it turns a broken display into a handled case.

steps.instruction: Before this goes near a class, one more thing that is not code.

rules.text: Write down ten real notes and the tag each should get.
Run all ten after every prompt change. Count how many are right.
rules.example: 8 of 10, and you know which two broke

rules.text: Keep the score. A change that fixes one and breaks two is a loss.

body: Without this, tuning a prompt is guessing, and you cannot tell improvement from noise.
Ten cases in a file is not a testing framework. It is thirty minutes that saves the feature.
steps.keypoint: Ten known inputs, run after every change. That is the whole discipline.

steps.instruction: Two of three tags matched. What does the score print?
steps.after: Two out of three. Change the prompt, run it again, and now you know if you helped.
steps.why: Two right. Run this after every prompt change and you can tell an improvement from a coincidence.

steps.instruction: The whole feature, in one function.
steps.after: Six steps, one function, and every failure has an answer. That is a feature, not a demo.
body: Guard, prompt, send, parse, check, show. Every failure has an answer.
